'''Paul F. J. Eagles''' is an Emeritus Professor at the [[University of Waterloo]] in Canada.<ref>{{cite web |title=Paul F. J. Eagles |url=https://uwaterloo.ca/recreation-and-leisure-studies/people-profiles/paul-eagles |website=People profiles |publisher=University of Waterloo |access-date=17 February 2021}}</ref> He is a Biologist and a Planner, specializing in [[environmental planning]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/thestar/access/433020081.html?FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Jan+08%2C+2000&author=Bob+Burtt&pub=Waterloo+Region+Record&desc=Taking+the+authority+out+of+conservation%3B+Debilitating+provincial+cuts+endanger+our+natural+areas&pqatl=google|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121106211350/http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/thestar/access/433020081.html?FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Jan+08,+2000&author=Bob+Burtt&pub=Waterloo+Region+Record&desc=Taking+the+authority+out+of+conservation%3B+Debilitating+provincial+cuts+endanger+our+natural+areas&pqatl=google|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 6, 2012|title=Taking the authority out of conservation; Debilitating provincial cuts endanger our natural areas|last=Burtt|first=Bob|date=January 8, 2000|work=[[Waterloo Region Record]]|page=H1|quote=You have to look at why they are selling off Laurel Creek," says Paul Eagles, a University of Waterloo professor of environmental planning....|accessdate=28 May 2011}}</ref>

Over a span of 30 years, Eagles worked on a wide variety of planning projects, with an especially strong emphasis on the planning and management of parks and [[protected area]]s. Since the mid-1980s he undertook international work in nature-based tourism and park tourism, with experience in over 25 countries. Since 1996 he has been the Chair of the Task Force on Tourism and Protected Areas for the [[World Commission on Protected Areas]], of [[World Conservation Union]] based in Switzerland. In May 2002, Eagles co-authored the book, ''Sustainable Tourism in Protected Areas: Guidelines for Planning and Management''. This was co-published by the World Conservation Union, the [[World Tourism Organization]] and [[United Nations|the United Nations]] Environment Programme as a contribution to the UN Year of [[Ecotourism]]. In November 2002 Professor Eagles, in cooperation with Dr. Stephen McCool of [[the University of Montana]], published his 15th book, entitled: ''Tourism in National Parks and Protected Areas: Planning and Management''.

He has over 330 publications, including 17 books.
